chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man who deliberately broke the fast one day in the month of Ramadan, and he said:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said, “I am ruined, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “What is the matter with you?” He said, “The Fire, O Messenger of Allah.” He said, “And what is the matter with you?” He said, “I had intercourse with my wife.” So he said, “Give charity and seek forgiveness from your Lord.” The man said, “By the One who has magnified your right, I have left nothing in the house, neither little nor much.” He said: Then a man from the people entered with a basket of dates containing twenty sa's. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him, “Take these dates and give them in charity.” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I give them in charity, when I have informed you that there is nothing in my house, neither little nor much?” He said, “Then take it and feed it to your dependents, and seek forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” He said: When we went out, our companions said, “He began with emancipation.” He said, “Free a slave, or fast, or give charity.”

key_terms.الْعِتْقِ: emancipation of a slave as a form of expiation
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, during which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.وَقَعْتُ عَلَى أَهْلِي: I had intercourse with my wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who deliberately breaks a Ramadan fast through intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan through intercourse. It shows a legal ruling alongside mercy and practical accommodation for one who is unable to fulfill the expiation immediately, while still emphasizing charity and seeking forgiveness.
